strategy: First probe whether near-limit memory pressure can destabilize a checkout dependency, then test a controlled packet-loss failure on the revenue path and CPU sensitivity in the all-flow cart service. These cover resource exhaustion, errors/latency, and slowdown while avoiding repeated experiments whose outcomes are already well established.

spec.reason: shippingservice is a single replica with a 128Mi memory limit and serves view_cart and checkout. A prior 100MB stress run completed without user impact; 120MB tests closer to the limit for a short duration and answers whether that apparent headroom persists.
spec.hypothesis: At 120MB, memory pressure may cause shippingservice to become unavailable or restart, affecting checkout and possibly view_cart; the guard may stop the experiment if errors exceed its threshold.

experiments.learning_goal: Does shippingservice tolerate memory pressure near its container limit, or does it OOM/restart and disrupt its user flows?

spec.reason: cartservice is a single replica with a 300m CPU limit, is shared by checkoutservice and frontend, and has reach across all five flows. A prior 80% CPU-stress run was externally interrupted after 16 seconds and showed substantial slowdown without errors, so this lower controlled load tests sensitivity without simply repeating that intensity.
spec.hypothesis: CPU contention will slow flows that call cartservice, potentially most of the shop, but at 40% load should remain below the safety guard and produce few or no errors.

experiments.learning_goal: How much does moderate CPU contention in the shared cart service propagate across the shop before it causes errors or guard-level latency?

spec.reason: paymentservice is a single replica on the checkout path, so this isolates a revenue-critical dependency without exposing every flow. Past runs tested paymentservice unavailability, but not partial packet loss; the low-loss setting also differs from the already-tested 5% currencyservice loss.
spec.hypothesis: A small amount of packet loss may trigger retries and slow checkout, but should not cause broad shop impact or exceed the default guard thresholds during this short run.

experiments.learning_goal: Does partial network impairment of paymentservice turn into checkout errors or retries and latency, even when the service is not fully unavailable?

skipped_ideas.idea: Repeat a frontend traffic spike around 100–300 users
skipped_ideas.why_not: Past runs already characterize this range: 100–150 users completed with substantial slowdown, while repeated 300-user runs approached or crossed the 1500ms guard.
Repeated runs show this affects all five flows with roughly 700ms p95; it is already known, and higher intensities have repeatedly tripped the guard.
Prior redis-cart failure and cartservice pod-kill runs already show severe, broad impact and rapid guard activation or long recovery; repeating these would add little to the current learning goals.
